headline: Dollar Tree comps rose 5% on higher tickets as traffic fell; its 2026 EPS outlook came in a bit below consensus.

metrics.comp_label: Dollar Tree comparable store net sales (continuing ops)

guidance_note: FY26: sales $20.5-20.7bn, comps +3-4%, adj. EPS $6.50-6.90 (midpoint below ~$6.74 consensus); Q1 EPS $1.45-1.60.
key_messages: Comps +5.0%: ticket +6.3%, traffic -1.2%; January weather closures cost ~40 bps.
Discretionary comps +6.2% vs consumables +3.6%; Christmas, party, paper and toys strong.
Gross margin +150 bps to 39.1% on pricing mark-on and lower freight, despite tariff costs and markdowns.
Multi-price items ($3-5) driving demand; about 16% of Q4 sales.
Creedon: pack sizes help lower-income shoppers manage budgets.

consumer.income_split: Management highlighted smaller pack sizes to help lower-income shoppers manage tight budgets.
consumer.big_ticket: Discretionary comps of 6.2% led by holiday, party and toys.
consumer.pricing: Pricing initiatives and multi-price mark-on lifted margin; tariff costs partly offset; managing tariff volatility.

macro_read: Holiday discretionary spending at the low end held up, but fewer trips and higher tickets point to price-driven rather than volume-driven growth.
